Trench: over 40 ft → combine service + load in one conduit (100–125 A services only).
40 ft or less → keep separate.
150/200 A → always two conduits.
•    Clay tile / metal roof / no attic run: no J-box under the soffit.
Hard pipe in EMT from load center to array, and show it that way on the elevation.
•    BOS for those roofs: must include EMT (3/4"–1"), fittings, LB and conduit hangers.
 Wires are THWN (#10 red/black, #8 green), not Romex.
Roof boxes stay on the BOM.
•    No PVC on roofs.
•    Disconnect height: max 6'7" to the top breaker / disconnect handle, not to the top of the enclosure.
•    Conduit: use LB. Keep covers accessible.
•    Door offset with two conduits: use 8 × 45° + 12 couplings.

1- In one raceway we can't exceed 360 degrees of bend without adding LB (conduit body)
2- 4/0 is hard to pull when we have too many conduit bodies so it's better to use 2/0 CU in these cases
3- For 200A/150A service let's use AL and for 125/100 service let's use is CU unless we need SER.
4- SER is rated for outdoor as long its not subject to physical damage
7- Service wires:
- 4/0 SER for attic runs
- 2/0 CU for exterior conduit runs with bends
- 4/0 AL for straight exterior conduit runs

1- Make sure to check if the designers point out if the panels installed on the facing street roof.
2- Always make sure the that the designer provide the roof condition and rating
3- Always check if we have to cut concrete pad in case we have an existing concrete or limited space for the concrete pad.
